title: Jazmín Calimano Colón
text: Jazmín transitioned from scientific research, holding a B.S. in Chemistry, into the civic tech space to merge her technical background with her dedication to community building. Based in Chicago and pursuing a degree in Civic Analytics, she is passionate about leveraging data research with R to uncover insights, solve urban challenges, and elevate nonprofit and civic initiatives.

title: Past Projects Showcase
text:
May 2026

This project examines how socioeconomic hardship affects library visits across Chicago neighborhoods from 2013 to 2023. I used random forest modeling and k-means clustering in R to identify factors associated with library visitation and explore geographic disparities in library access across Chicago communities.
 Download Full Report (PDF) 

Exploratory Data AnalysisCluster InsightsChicago Map





The scatterplot shows a negative trend between a community’s hardship index and the average annual visits to their local libraries. As hardship in a community increases, residents are less likely to use library services. This indicates that economic difficulties may reduce community involvement with library resources.







This chart shows how the three clusters compare to the city average.







Spatial distribution of clusters using Leaflet.

title: Past Projects Showcase
text:
This report looks at conference attendance and feedback in London, Washington, D.C., and Toronto to find trends in engagement and attendee experience. I used Microsoft Excel to analyze the data and identify patterns, then created clear visualizations with Canva to present the findings effectively.
This project shows my skills in data analysis, trend identification, and visual storytelling to support decision-making.
